entries.title: Transient State for High-Frequency Updates
entries.why: At 10 Hz updates across 3 rigs (30 updates/sec), using React state would cause 30 re-renders per second - way too many. Transient state is a plain object mutated directly, bypassing React entirely.
entries.whatItDoes: Defines transientState object with nested structure: rigs.A, rigs.B, rigs.C, each containing rpm, temperature, vibration, pressure, bearing_temp, anomalyScore, isRunning. Initial values are realistic defaults.
entries.perfNotes: Direct mutation = no React overhead. 3D useFrame reads this every frame.

entries.title: Ketchup Factory Transient State (25 Lines)
entries.why: The ketchup factory has 25 production lines, each with 6+ sensors. That's 250+ updates per second at 10 Hz - absolutely must bypass React for this scale.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates object with lines L01-L25 using Array.from() and Object.fromEntries(). Each line has: fill_level, viscosity, sauce_temp, cap_torque, bottle_flow_rate, label_alignment, bottle_count, anomaly_score, anomaly_type.
entries.perfNotes: 25 lines * 10 Hz = 250 direct mutations/sec - no problem for JS

entries.title: Transient State Accessors & Updaters
entries.why: These exported functions provide controlled access to transient state. Getters return the raw object for reading in useFrame. Updaters use Object.assign for efficient partial updates.
entries.whatItDoes: getTransientState(): Returns transientState object. updateTransientRig(rigId, data): Merges data into rigs[rigId]. getKetchupTransientState(): Returns ketchupTransientState. updateKetchupLine(lineId, data): Merges data into lines[lineId].

failureModes.recovery: Updates for unknown IDs are silently ignored

entries.perfNotes: Object.assign is faster than spread for partial updates

entries.title: Zustand Store for UI State
entries.why: UI state that SHOULD trigger re-renders (connection status, alerts, selected rig) uses Zustand. It's minimal React state for things that need UI updates.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates Zustand store with subscribeWithSelector middleware (enables selective subscriptions). Initial state: connected=false, connectionError=null, selectedRig=null, viewMode='rig', alerts=[], maxAlerts=10, systemStatus object.
entries.perfNotes: subscribeWithSelector avoids unnecessary re-renders from unrelated state changes

entries.title: Zustand Actions for State Updates
entries.why: Zustand actions encapsulate state mutations. They're called from event handlers and UI components to update connection status, alerts, selection, etc.
entries.whatItDoes: Actions include: setConnected/setConnectionError (connection state), setLastUpdate (timestamp), setSelectedRig/clearSelectedRig (rig selection), setSelectedKetchupLine/clearSelectedKetchupLine, setViewMode, toggleDebug/togglePause, addAlert (prepends and limits to maxAlerts), clearAlerts, dismissAlert (filters by ID), setSystemStatus.
entries.perfNotes: addAlert uses slice(0, maxAlerts) to cap array size

entries.title: Alert Management Logic
entries.why: Alerts need unique IDs (for dismissal), timestamps (for display), and capping (prevent memory leaks). The addAlert action handles all of this.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates new alert with: id (Date.now()), timestamp (ISO string), plus spread of input alert data. Prepends to alerts array (newest first). Slices to maxAlerts (10) to prevent unbounded growth. dismissAlert filters out by ID.
entries.perfNotes: Array slice + spread is efficient for small arrays (< 100)

entries.title: Computed Getters for Alert State
entries.why: Components often need derived values like 'how many alerts?' or 'any critical alerts?'. Computed getters provide these without storing redundant state.
entries.whatItDoes: getAlertCount(): Returns alerts.length. hasActiveAlerts(): Returns true if any alert has severity='critical'. These call get() to access current state within the getter.
entries.perfNotes: Getters are computed on demand, not cached
